cands.name: Donald J. Mottern

top: St Clair County Democratic Executive Committee
money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.

cands.bio: Donald Mottern is a journalist and former writer for the Shelby County Reporter, with Alabama Press Association awards. He has also been a small business owner and has worked in the hotel, food service and mortgage industries. He holds a University of Alabama degree (2017). He has not held public office.

Alabama Cannabis Coalition (listed among his endorsements and voter-guide recommendations)

cands.gaps: We found no record of Mottern holding public office, so there is no legislative track record to report. We found no stated position from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land conservation, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, abortion, school vouchers or teacher pay, or police pay. He names immigration as an area of interest but gives no specific position. We found no documented public stance on data centers or development, and no foreign ties or controversies. His specific job dates and employers beyond the Shelby County Reporter were not available.

second-amendment.evidence: Says he fully supports the Second Amendment and owns firearms, and opposes banning assault weapons and sawed-off shotguns. He also says he supports background checks, barring people with a history of violence or domestic abuse from owning guns, and the existing ban on fully automatic weapons.

top: Poarch Creek Band Of Creek Indians PAC
money.note: Covers January 2023 on, primary and general. Party-committee lines are often in-kind staff and mail.

cands.bio: Attorney and Republican member of the Alabama State Senate for District 11 since November 9, 2022. Former Pell City prosecutor, partner at a law firm, and investigator in the St. Clair County District Attorney's Office. Chaired the St. Clair County Republican Party.
cands.gaps: We could not find where Lance Bell was born or raised, or when he came to Alabama. We found no statements from him on data centers, development, property taxes, immigration, guns, abortion, schools or policing, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2022 or 2026. The sponsored-bills list on his Ballotpedia page was empty in the copy we read, so we could not confirm any bills he sponsored. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or notable endorsements.
